meta.dataset: Punctual Pros weather-to-service-call demand model (HVAC / plumbing / electrical), NWS alert playbook, territory zone codes and weather hubs
meta.method: Baselines are derived from national homeowner surveys (American Home Shield 2024 share of homeowners calling each trade; Census American Housing Survey breakdown incidence; DuraPlas maintenance survey) converted to calls/day per 10k households with stated visit-frequency assumptions. Weather multipliers use ServiceTitan heat-wave elasticities (+20% calls, +25% jobs, +55–90% revenue) and NWS/Consumer Reports thresholds; magnitudes without a public elasticity are labeled "assumption" with rationale. Local exceedance frequencies were computed from NOAA GHCN-Daily (2019–2025) for hub stations, event-history counts from NOAA Storm Events, and zone/UGC codes and hub grid metadata were pulled live from api.weather.gov.

formula.expected_calls[trade,county,day]: baseline_per_10k[trade] x households[county]/10,000 x month_index[trade,month] x max(weather multipliers active for trade that day, with 0.5 x each additional independent driver above 1.0) x housing_age_modifier
formula.pp_expected_calls: expected_calls x PP_market_share[county] (parameter; set from PP booked-call history / ServiceTitan data)
formula.combination_rule_basis: assumption — avoids double counting correlated drivers (e.g., heat + humidity)
formula.multiplier_point_estimate: use midpoint of range until calibrated
formula.calibration: Regress PP daily booked calls by trade on TMAX/TMIN/PRCP/WSF5 from the hub stations (GHCN-Daily) and NWS alert flags; replace assumption ranges with fitted elasticities once 12+ months of PP data are loaded.

sources_summary: ServiceTitan (heat-wave study; State of the Trades after-hours data)
US Census Bureau American Housing Survey brief (1999)
ACHR News (DuraPlas maintenance survey; service agreements)
National Weather Service (weather.gov product definitions, LWX criteria, api.weather.gov zones/points/alert types)
NOAA NCEI GHCN-Daily and Storm Events
meta.nws_product_naming_note: api.weather.gov/alerts/types (retrieved 2026-09-24) lists "Extreme Heat Warning/Watch" and "Extreme Cold Warning/Watch" and "Cold Weather Advisory"; the legacy names Excessive Heat Warning and Wind Chill Warning/Advisory no longer appear — portal filters should match both names for historical alerts.
caveats: No public source gives calls per 10k households directly; baselines are derived market-wide totals across all providers and must be multiplied by PP market share, which is unknown (parameter).

Most plumbing and electrical multipliers and all heating multipliers are assumptions (clearly labeled) — only the cooling heat-wave effect has a published multi-shop elasticity (ServiceTitan, national, 2019–2021; Northeast not broken out).
County household counts were not embedded: the Census ACS API now requires a key; the portal should join ACS B11001 households by county_fips.

Climatology station proxies: Carlisle/Lebanon use Harrisburg Intl; Chambersburg/Gettysburg use York Airport; Toms River uses Atlantic City Intl (Lakehurst NAS daily record too sparse); Freehold COOP station has no wind-gust data.
NWS local warning criteria for CTP (State College) and PHI (Mt Holly) were not retrievable; LWX (Sterling) criteria are used as the regional reference for heat/wind thresholds.
Companion dataset /Users/syed/BSP/data/research/pp_storm_events.json holds the county-month storm history this model references.

items.scope: market-wide reactive (repair/no-heat/no-cool) calls to all providers, annualized average day; excludes planned maintenance
items.derivation: 26% of homeowners called an HVAC technician in the past year (American Home Shield survey, Nov 2024, n=993) x assumed 1.1–1.8 visits per calling household = 0.29–0.47 calls/household/yr -> 10,000 x (0.29–0.47)/365 = 7.8–12.8/day. Housecall Pro platform data: ~88% of HVAC jobs in Q1 2026 were repairs.

planned_maintenance_addon.derivation: 30% of homeowners schedule preventive HVAC maintenance (DuraPlas/Pollfish, Jun 2023) x 1–2 visits/yr -> 8.2–16.4 per 10k households/day; schedulable, not weather-driven

assumptions: visits per calling household 1.1–1.8 (assumption: repair + return/parts visit)
survey skews to homeowners; renters call landlords

items.scope: market-wide residential service/repair calls (leaks, clogs, water heaters, toilets, sewer)
items.derivation: 52% of homeowners called a plumber in the past year (American Home Shield, Nov 2024) x 1.0–1.5 visits = 0.52–0.78/household/yr -> 14–21/day per 10k households. Floor cross-check from Census American Housing Survey 1999: inside water leak 10% of households/12 mo; all-toilets-down 3%, water-supply stoppage 4%, sewer/septic breakdown 2% per 3 months -> ~0.35–0.45 serious incidents/household/yr (~10–12/day per 10k) before routine clogs/water-heater work. Housecall Pro: ~87% of plumbing jobs were repairs.

items.scope: market-wide residential electrical service calls (outages in home, breakers, outlets, surge damage, generator); excludes planned projects such as panel upgrades and EV chargers
items.derivation: 27% of homeowners called an electrician in the past year (American Home Shield, Nov 2024) x 1.0–1.3 visits = 0.27–0.35/household/yr -> 7.4–9.6/day per 10k households; discounted toward 5 because part of electrician demand is project work. AHS 1999: 11% of households had fuses blown/breakers tripped in the past 3 months (27% of those 3+ times), mostly DIY resets -> latent demand pool.

items.notes: Samsara telematics (65M HVAC service trips, Sep 2023–Jun 2025): October is the busiest month nationally (heating start-up), July–October is primary demand season, a consistent September dip, February the annual low. ServiceTitan: off-hours share of inbound calls 14.1% in June vs 9.8% in October 2025 (after-hours weekday 9.3% vs 6.8%; weekend 4.9% Aug vs 2.95% Oct); off-hours peak 5–9 pm local.
items.portal_use: Scale baseline by month before applying weather multipliers; pull PP ServiceTitan/CRM history to replace with actual monthly index once available.

items.rule: Breakdown incidence rises with housing age: pre-1940 homes vs 1990s homes: fuses/breakers 14% vs 9%, uncomfortably cold last winter 11% vs 6%, water leak from outside 20% vs 9% (AHS 1999 Table 1). Apply 1.2–1.5x to baselines for ZIPs with median year built < 1960 (Lancaster/Reading/York/Harrisburg city cores).

items.driver: daily max temperature (TMAX) at nearest hub station

piecewise.condition: heat wave: >=2 consecutive days unusually hot with warm nights (EPA/ServiceTitan definition), approx TMAX>=90F and TMIN>=70F
piecewise.note: ServiceTitan (~800 HVAC shops, 2019–2021): heat waves raised daily calls +20%, jobs +25%, revenue +55%

piecewise.condition: TMAX >= 95F or heat index >= 105F (Extreme Heat Warning territory)
piecewise.note: extrapolated beyond ServiceTitan average; ticket mix shifts to replacements/refrigerant

season_sequence_decay.basis: derived: ServiceTitan revenue uplift by heat-wave order 90%/55%/40%/20%/~0% normalized to first wave

items.after_hours_share_shift: +4 to +5 pts of calls after hours in peak summer (ServiceTitan 14.1% Jun vs 9.8% Oct)
items.note_humidity: Casselman & Karamperidou (Nature Communications 2026): humidity-adjusted "effective CDD" rises 7.5–15% faster than conventional CDD over much of the US; use heat index, not just TMAX, for the warning tier.

items.driver: daily cooling degree days (base 65F, NWS definition: mean temp minus 65)
items.rationale: CDD is the standard proxy for cooling load (NWS/EIA); thresholds chosen so CDD>15 (mean >80F, roughly TMAX>=90F with warm night) aligns with the ServiceTitan heat-wave tier. Recalibrate with PP call logs.

items.driver: daily minimum temperature (TMIN) / heating degree days

piecewise.condition: first cold snap of season (first day HDD >= 25, i.e. mean <= 40F, after Oct 1)
piecewise.note: no-heat start-up failures; Samsara shows October national peak driven by heating reactivation

items.rationale: No public dataset quantifies no-heat call elasticity; tiers mirror the cooling side and the AHS finding that 7% of households were uncomfortably cold in the prior winter. Samsara documents that a ~10F seasonal drop triggers heating-system service spikes.

items.driver: hard freeze: TMIN <= 20F for >= 2 consecutive days

piecewise.condition: thaw day (first TMAX > 40F after hard freeze) — bursts discovered as ice melts

items.threshold_source: Consumer Reports: frozen pipes generally occur below 20F (earlier in uninsulated spaces); IBHS: burst pipes are among the most common cold-weather property losses.

piecewise.note: sump pump failure, basement seepage, sewer/drain backup

items.rationale: AHS 1999: 12% of households had water leak in from outside within 12 months (13% owners); older stock ~2x. Flash floods are the #2 event type by count in the PP territory (Storm Events 2019–2025, peak July).

piecewise.condition: gust >= 58 mph (NWS severe / High Wind criteria)

items.rationale: Tree/limb contact with service drops and weatherheads, then restoration surges. Climate Central: 80% of major US outages 2000–2023 were weather-related; severe weather (wind, rain, thunderstorms) 58%, winter weather 23%, tropical 14%; Pennsylvania ranked 9th nationally (82 outages). NWS High Wind criteria: sustained 40 mph for 1h or gusts 58 mph.

items.driver: utility outage affecting > 5% of customers in a county (from utility outage map / PowerOutage feeds)

piecewise.note: generator installs/repairs, restoration-surge damage, meter-base/mast repairs required before utility reconnect

items.rationale: Outage-driven demand is well documented qualitatively; no public elasticity. Winter outages also lift HVAC (no-heat) and plumbing (freeze) calls.

items.driver: lightning / Severe Thunderstorm Warning with CG lightning in county

piecewise.condition: documented lightning strike damage in Storm Events
piecewise.note: surge-damaged panels, GFCIs, HVAC control boards

items.rationale: III: 61,986 US homeowners lightning claims in 2025 ($1.649B, avg $26,616); Pennsylvania #8 with 2,177 claims ($33.4M, avg $15,355). Thunderstorm Wind is the #1 Storm Events type in PP territory (peak Jun–Jul).

items.lead_time: 12–24 h (LWX criteria: heat index >=110F east of Blue Ridge within 12–24 h); Extreme Heat Watch 24–72 h
actions: Move all HVAC maintenance visits off the schedule; convert to repair capacity
Extend dispatch to 10–12 h shifts + on-call after-hours rotation (5–9 pm peak)
Pre-stage capacitors, contactors, condenser fan motors, R-410A/R-454B, hard-start kits on every truck
Triage: elderly/medical households first; offer portable AC loaners
CSR overflow + callback SLA; pause non-emergency outbound marketing
